text: Bug #1 (relativedelta with whole-number floats for years/months): confirmed. `relativedelta(months=1.0)` passes the integral check but keeps the float, so `datetime(2000,1,1) + relativedelta(months=1.0)` blows up (TypeError from calendar.monthrange). Fixing it so integral floats are treated as the equivalent int. ETA ~12 min.

Bug #2 (rrule count=0): confirmed — `count=0` is falsy in `_iter`, so it is treated as "no limit" and generates up to year 9999 (count() == 8003). Fixing so count=0 yields no occurrences and count() == 0. ETA ~15 min.

Bug #3 (missing `RRULE:` prefix in str(rrule)): confirmed — `__str__` joins the parts without the property name, so the output is not RFC2445-compliant and does not round-trip through rrulestr as documented. Adding the `RRULE:` prefix. ETA ~15 min.

Bug #4 (fuzzy parse of a URL): confirmed — the lone `p` matches the AM/PM marker and is swallowed by the AM/PM branch instead of being reported as a skipped token. Fixing so fuzzy parsing skips it and returns the correct datetime plus the full leftover text. ETA ~18 min.

Bug #5 (parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True) raising IndexError): confirmed — the HH:MM[:SS] branch indexes l[i+1] without checking it exists, so a trailing colon escapes as an IndexError instead of being ignored. Fixing the bounds check so the trailing colon is skipped and datetime(2017,7,17,6,15) is returned. ETA ~8 min.

Status of the earlier ones: #2 (rrule count=0) and #3 (RRULE: prefix) are fixed and verified (full suite still 1064 passed / 43 skipped). #1 and #4 are fixed in the working tree and being verified now.

Bug #6 (relativedelta + relativedelta dropping explicit zeros): confirmed — `__add__`/`__sub__` merge the absolute attributes (year/month/day/weekday/hour/minute/second/microsecond) with `or`, so an explicitly-set 0 is treated as "unset". Fixing both operators to use None-checks so `relativedelta() + relativedelta(day=0, hour=0)` keeps day=0, hour=0. ETA ~8 min.

Status: #2, #3, #4, #5 are fixed and verified (full suite still 1064 passed / 43 skipped); #1 is fixed and verified too.

Bug #1 fixed and verified: integral floats for years/months are now coerced to int, so `datetime(2000,1,1) + relativedelta(months=1.0)` == `datetime(2000,2,1)` and `years=1.0` gives `datetime(2001,1,1)`; non-integral values (e.g. 1.5) still raise the same ValueError. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.

Bug #2 fixed and verified: `count=0` is now honored as a real limit, so `rrule(YEARLY, count=0, dtstart=...)` yields no occurrences and `rr.count()` == 0 (count=1/2/3 still yield exactly that many). Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.

Bug #3 fixed and verified: `str(rrule(...))` now emits `DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=5`, matching the documented RFC2445 form and round-tripping through rrulestr. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.

Bug #4 fixed and verified: `parse('http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/600221.html', fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` now returns `(datetime(2060, 2, 21, 0, 0), ('http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/', '.html'))` — the stray `p` is reported as skipped text instead of being consumed as an AM/PM marker. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.

Bug #5 fixed and verified: `parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True)` now returns `datetime(2017, 7, 17, 6, 15)` (the trailing colon is skipped) instead of failing; `HH:MM:SS` and non-fuzzy behavior are unchanged. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.

Bug #6 fixed and verified: `relativedelta() + relativedelta(day=0, hour=0)` and the reverse order now both give `relativedelta(day=0, hour=0)`; `__add__` and `__sub__` use None-checks for the absolute attributes so explicitly-set zeros survive. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.
